correctness.rationale: Disjoint supports give an exact product quasi-norm identity. For nonzero lambda this makes T_lambda injective and bounded below, hence with closed range. The block sets M_i identify each range slice with span{lambda}; choosing e_r outside that line yields infinitely many independent quotient classes. For any N-dimensional W, every positive iterate maps into ran(T_lambda), so the quotient image of the whole orbit is q(W), a finite-dimensional closed subspace of an infinite-dimensional Hausdorff quotient and therefore cannot be dense. This handles all p>0 and both scalar fields without experiments.

value.rationale: The source itself places isometric copies of non-cyclic operators and N-supercyclic spaceability side by side. The accepted result connects those themes by showing that the canonical isometric copy already avoids every finite supercyclicity level at once, while upgrading non-dense range to closed infinite-codimensional range. The conclusion is structural and simultaneous rather than a routine numerical refinement.
